classification.description: Semantic roles this platform assigns to columns — what a column *is*, independent of what it was named in the source. Drives review coverage, PII handling and the semantic layer.
classification.name: PlatformRole

glossary.description: Business vocabulary projected from this platform's ontology (version 2). Generated by `pf openmetadata sync` — edit `platform/src/pf/ontology/concepts.yaml`, not the catalogue.
glossary.name: Platform Ontology

| `status` | string | status_enum | no |

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A monetary amount without its currency is not a number, it is a bug waiting for a second entity to be onboarded.

**Constraint:** `sibling_role_present`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.ontology.validate:money-without-currency

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_money-requires-currency

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A class with no identity property cannot participate in a derived join, so every BI and MDL projection of it is a guess.

**Constraint:** `identity_declared`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.ontology.validate:class-without-identity

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_entity-requires-identity

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A foreign key pointing at a class the topology does not relate to is an undeclared join. Undeclared joins are how two teams compute different revenue from the same warehouse.

**Constraint:** `relation_exists`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.ontology.validate:illegal-edge

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_link-must-be-in-topology

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** PII may land in raw and staging. It must not reach a mart or an exposure without a masking policy or an explicit, recorded waiver.

**Constraint:** `not_in_layer`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.loops.registry:pii_audit

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_pii-not-in-consumption

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** Grain is the one fact a downstream consumer cannot infer and cannot survive guessing. An undeclared grain is how a join silently fans out.

**Constraint:** `meta_field_present`

**Severity:** warning

**Enforced by:** pf.kg.build:model-grain

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_mart-declares-grain

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** Aggregation policy — which statuses count, which timestamp, which filter — belongs to exactly one metric definition. A mart column named `revenue` is a second definition that will drift from the first.

**Constraint:** `no_metric_shaped_columns`

**Severity:** warning

**Enforced by:** pf.ontology.validate:metric-shaped-column

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_metric-owns-aggregation

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A model or column change must report what it breaks before it lands, including the human who owns each affected exposure.

**Constraint:** `impact_reported`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** platform/hooks/pre_tool_use.py, platform/hooks/pre_commit.sh

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_change-declares-blast-radius

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A blast radius is a prediction made from lineage. Lineage cannot say whether the numbers actually moved, so a change to a mart must also be compared against a built baseline before it lands — otherwise "safe" means "nothing downstream references it", not "nothing downstream changed".

**Constraint:** `diff_reported`

**Severity:** warning

**Enforced by:** pf.tools.recce:dagster_assets, pf.tools.recce:register_commands

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_change-verified-against-baseline

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A value-level diff writes the rows it compared into the review tool's state file, which is durable and shared. Diffing a column whose role is PII therefore persists real addresses into an artefact that gets committed and passed around — the same failure `pii-not-in-consumption` prevents in the warehouse, one layer further out.

**Constraint:** `pii_excluded_from_review`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.ontology.model:Role.review_intent, pf.tools.recce:generate_config

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_review-artifacts-exclude-pii

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A dbt build that leaves no queryable record cannot be triaged; failures get diagnosed from whichever log happened to survive. Every build must record its run and test results into the warehouse with history — for every test framework at once — so "is this new, recurring, or flaky?" is a query, not an archaeology dig.

**Constraint:** `observability_recorded`

**Severity:** warning

**Enforced by:** pf.tools.elementary:bootstrap_project, pf.tools.elementary:ensure_package

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_builds-record-observability

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** Hand-written test coverage decays to whichever models someone remembered. The floor — an annotated mart is never empty, a declared identity identifies — must be derived from the ontology roles, so coverage is a function of annotation rather than of memory, and a wrong test is a wrong role rather than a stale file.

**Constraint:** `tests_derived_from_roles`

**Severity:** warning

**Enforced by:** pf.tools.expectations:write_tests, pf.tools.expectations:bootstrap_project

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_quality-floor-derived-from-ontology

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A credential placed in a prompt, a model file or a committed artefact is durably persisted and replayed into every later session.

**Constraint:** `path_denied`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** gate.yaml:denylist, platform/hooks/pre_tool_use.py

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_secrets-never-in-context

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** An agent reaches the filesystem through one path gate, and the paths it may never write are declared rather than remembered. Least privilege that lives in a prompt is a request; in a denylist it is a control.

**Constraint:** `path_denied`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** gate.yaml:denylist, gate.yaml:platform_denylist, pf.loops.gate:check_path

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_agent-authority-is-least-privilege

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A tool contributes gate rules, and a plugin system that can widen the policy judging it is not a policy. `Tool.gate_sections()` rejects a contribution to any loosening section at construction, so an unsafe tool fails at import rather than silently permitting more.

**Constraint:** `tightening_only`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.tools.spec:Tool.gate_sections

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_tool-contribution-may-only-tighten

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** Every tool call an agent makes is written down before it happens and after it happens, and the gate's verdict is recorded for allows as well as denies. "No rule applied" and "a rule allowed it" are different facts, and only a record that carries both can answer what an agent was permitted to do.

**Constraint:** `action_recorded`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.provenance.ledger:decision, platform/hooks/pre_tool_use.py, platform/hooks/post_tool_use.py

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_agent-decisions-are-recorded

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A log an agent can edit is not evidence. Each record carries the hash of the one before it, and the head is anchored to a timestamp authority with no stake in what it says — so editing the middle requires editing the end, and the end is countersigned.

**Constraint:** `hash_chained`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.provenance.chain:verify, pf.provenance.anchor:stamp_rfc3161, gate.yaml:denylist

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_evidence-chain-is-tamper-evident

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** Business logic does not transfer between entities, so an assumption carried from one sister company into another is a bug by construction. A project session may not read or write another project, and may not write shared infra at all.

**Constraint:** `cross_tenant_denied`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** gate.yaml:platform_denylist, pf.loops.gate:project_for

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_sister-projects-are-isolated

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A control that cannot be switched off mid-incident is a control you find out about afterwards. Revocation is checked before intent is written, and an unreadable revocation file fails closed.

**Constraint:** `revocable`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.provenance.ledger:revoke, pf.provenance.ledger:is_revoked

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_agent-authority-is-revocable

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** Human oversight is a chain that shows the approval, not a document that asserts it. Approvals are append-only and bound to the action they approve, and an actor approving their own action is a finding rather than an approval.

**Constraint:** `approval_recorded`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.provenance.ledger:approve, pf.provenance.audit:report

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_high-impact-actions-need-a-human

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** Which model answers which step is a declared table, not whatever the caller passed. An unregistered step is recorded as such, and the recorded verdict matches what actually happened rather than what policy would have preferred.

**Constraint:** `routing_declared`

**Severity:** warning

**Enforced by:** pf.agents.base:AGENTS

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_model-routing-is-declared

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** Every upstream this platform borrowed from carries a licence, and some of them constrain what we may ship. The review is written down per upstream and surfaced in the listing, so a constraint is a fact in the registry rather than something someone once checked.

**Constraint:** `licence_reviewed`

**Severity:** warning

**Enforced by:** pf.vendor.model:load_registry, pf.vendor.verify:verify

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_upstream-licences-are-reviewed

glossary_terms.description:
**Intent:** A risk register that names controls nobody enforces is a document. Each entity declares in `air.yaml` which controls it commits to; those are derived from the repository on every run and block the merge when they fail, while everything outside the baseline is reported and does not.

**Constraint:** `baseline_declared`

**Severity:** error

**Enforced by:** pf.air.coverage:assess, pf.air.register:render_register

_This is a data constraint from the platform's policy layer, not an OpenMetadata access-control policy._
glossary_terms.name: policy_control-baseline-is-declared
